One commenter said they don't want to proxy LLM calls through a third party, unless it is a gateway like LiteLLM, or store prompts in a SaaS. For tracing they use OTEL libraries, which they find sufficient.

Workaround: a blog post said Langfuse's LLM-as-judge isn't available in the free/self-hosted version. A commenter replied that you can add LLM-as-judge to self-hosted Langfuse by defining your own external evaluation pipeline.

NonBioS evaluated Langsmith, Lunary, Phoenix Arize, Portkey, Datadog and Helicone and picked Langfuse. They are still on v2.7, which 'works pretty good for us', and are not looking to upgrade to v3. They feel prompt evaluation needs a dedicated tool rather than an observability product.

One team installed both Langfuse and Phoenix and chose Langfuse because of Python dependency version conflicts with Phoenix. They liked that Langfuse only depended on Postgres, but noted the scalable v3 version requires more dependencies. They preferred Phoenix's use of OpenTelemetry.

'IMO it is one of the best solutions I've looked at.' This user appreciates the dedication to self-hosting, because keeping traces with sensitive customer data on an external company's server isn't practical for them.

While triaging LLM observability, dataset and eval tools at work, one user found Langfuse was the second solution they tried. It was 'simple enough to get set up locally with my existing stack for me to stop looking.'

One team has used Langfuse for about 6 months for LLMOps. SDKs are limited to Python and TypeScript, but the OpenAPI spec is easy to implement in any language. Being OSS was a reason they chose it. They use only part of the product, choosing via the API what to outsource, and appreciate that it's not opinionated.
'Been using this product for 5ish months, love the iteration and how the team reacts to feedback. The prompt versioning has been immensely valuable!'

AINews describes itself as happy adopters and calls Langfuse a comprehensive, intuitive open source solution. Pain point: retries for Instructor-style structured outputs mess up the traces, and they'd like them tracked and collapsible. Drafting-style workflows are also noisy in a chat flow.

One user ran self-hosted Langfuse via LiteLLM in a Jupyter notebook for synthetic data experiments. Having traces and scores in a unified browser UI made sanity-checking easier. However, the trace/generation retrieval API was 'brutally slow' for bulk scanning, so they queried the DB directly.
'It gave me sanity into otherwise very complex LLM infrastructure. We spend 60k+ every month on LLM calls, so having the backbone to debug when things go haywire has helped a lot.'
'Been using Langfuse OSS for almost 15 months from the start. By far the best solution. No dark patterns found in other projects such as Portkey.'
'maybe clickhouse can finally make sense of the langfuse documentation'
One commenter referred to 'the painful migration to Clickhouse from v2 to v3' for self-hosted Langfuse.
Anecdotally, in the London AI startup scene, one commenter doesn't know anyone who swears by Langfuse. They said no LLM tracing/monitoring tool they've used made them feel the way Honeycomb does.

A user who evaluated Langfuse for prompt management found it 'pretty behind in terms of features' and went with PromptLayer. They wanted a git-like API for versioning prompts, with metadata tagging, Jinja2, release labels and easy rollback. They added that 'Langfuse seemed way better at tracing though.'
'I personally migrated away from it to use Sentry, their software was honestly not that great.'

While evaluating the free version, one user struggled to implement Langfuse due to 'numerous bugs/confusing AI driven documentation.' The Ask AI-recommended approach for instrumenting Claude didn't work, and installation issues pushed them to consider another provider. They still say it's worth trying.

One team uses Langfuse for an internal doc analysis tool. They extract production generations into datasets to test edge cases, and use prompt folders to manage default prompts alongside user-customized prompts in the pipeline.
'Langfuse is by far the best of the langs (-chain, -graph, -smith, -flow) in terms of UI/DX/integration/docs/quality.'
